title: Provider-neutral Forge seam with a GitHub adapter
summary: Introduces a provider-neutral `Forge` trait (branch, pull request, status block, review, check status, head commit, capabilities) plus a pure `report_change` step that runs those calls in one fixed order, an in-memory `FakeForge` double, and a `GitHub` adapter that drives the existing `gh` command line. The `osf` CLI's review-post, status-apply and status-refresh paths now go through the trait instead of calling `gh` directly, and `pr_status` is split into a pure parser (`parse_checks`/`gates_from_checks`) with the process code moved into the adapter.

nodes.label: review post / review run --post-to
nodes.subtitle: review_post_cmd, post_run_outcome
nodes.summary: Builds the review plan, reads the head commit through the forge, and posts through `post_plan`, which now takes a `&dyn Forge` and returns a `PostedReview` or `ForgeError`.

nodes.label: pr status apply
nodes.subtitle: pr_status_apply_cmd
nodes.summary: Dry run still reads the body through the client; the real path now calls `forge.write_status_block` instead of reading and editing the body itself.

nodes.label: pr status refresh
nodes.subtitle: pr_status_refresh_cmd
nodes.summary: Gates now come from `forge.read_check_status` (or a checks JSON file), and the final write goes through `forge.write_status_block`.

nodes.label: github_adapter()
nodes.subtitle: the only place that builds GitHub<RealGh>
nodes.summary: Single construction point for the real adapter, so every command shares one wiring decision.

nodes.label: Forge trait
nodes.subtitle: create_branch, open_pull_request, write_status_block, post_review, read_check_status, head_commit, capabilities
nodes.summary: The seam between the factory and a code host. Object-safe and Send + Sync; nothing in the module names a provider.

nodes.label: Forge data types
nodes.subtitle: PullRequestId, NewReview, PostedReview, ReadOutcome, Capabilities
nodes.summary: Plain serializable request and result types, including `ReadOutcome` which tells 'found nothing' from 'could not read', and `VerdictCapability`/`ReadCapability` describing what the identity may do.

nodes.label: report_change
nodes.subtitle: open PR → status block → capabilities → review → checks
nodes.summary: Runs the Report step in one fixed order, stopping at the first failed step and naming it. Skips the post when a known verdict list omits the draft verdict; a Comment verdict always posts.

nodes.label: FakeForge
nodes.subtitle: in-memory double, records every call
nodes.summary: Records each call as plain data, can script per-operation answer sequences and failures, and performs no process, file, network or clock work.

nodes.label: GitHub<C> adapter
nodes.subtitle: impl Forge for GitHub<C: GhClient>
nodes.summary: Translates each trait method into `gh` invocations through the `GhClient` seam: API POSTs for branch and pull request, body read/apply/edit for the status block, review POST with self-review fallback, and check/login reads for capabilities.

nodes.label: RealGh
nodes.subtitle: GhClient over the gh process
nodes.summary: Spawns `gh` with piped stdin/stdout/stderr and returns the raw `GhOutput`; the only place that starts a process for the forge path.

nodes.label: pr_status parsing
nodes.subtitle: parse_checks, gates_from_checks
nodes.summary: The checks JSON reader is split into a pure `parse_checks` returning triples and `gates_from_checks` building the gate spec; `gates_from_checks_json` remains as a thin wrapper. The process code moved out to the adapter.

nodes.label: review plan/fallback
nodes.subtitle: payload, after_first_attempt, after_fallback_attempt
nodes.summary: Keeps the pure decision logic for what to send and how to react to a self-review refusal; `fetch_head_sha` and `post_via_gh` are removed, leaving only `fetch_diff` as a host read.

nodes.label: GitHub pull request host
nodes.subtitle: branches, PRs, reviews, checks
nodes.summary: The external code host the adapter drives; unchanged by this diff but the target of every forge call.
